front_blocks.md: Define **alternating current**.

back_blocks.md: An **alternating current** periodically varies from positive to negative and changes its magnitude continuously with time, with its direction reversing every half-cycle.

cards.back_md: An **alternating current** periodically varies from positive to negative and changes its magnitude continuously with time, with its direction reversing every half-cycle.

front_blocks.md: Define **peak current** (*I*<sub>0</sub>).

back_blocks.md: **Peak current** is the maximum value of the alternating current.

cards.back_md: **Peak current** is the maximum value of the alternating current.

front_blocks.md: What equation gives the value of an alternating current *I* at any time *t*?

back_blocks.md: $I = I_{0} \mathrm{sin} ( ω t )$

front_blocks.md: How is angular frequency *ω* related to time period *T* and frequency *f*?

back_blocks.md: $ω = \frac{2π}{T} = 2 π f$

front_blocks.md: The variation of alternating current or voltage with time can be described as a **..........** curve.

back_blocks.md: The variation of alternating current or voltage with time can be described as a **sinusoidal** curve.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Mains electricity is supplied as direct current.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Mains electricity is supplied as **alternating current** — this is the type of current produced by power stations and supplied to sockets.

front_blocks.md: How do electrons in a wire carrying alternating current move?

back_blocks.md: They move back and forth with **simple harmonic motion**.

back_blocks.md: The value of a constant (direct) current that produces the same power in a resistor as the alternating current.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A direct voltage produces a different amount of heating in a resistor compared to an alternating voltage of the same r.m.s. value.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
The **r.m.s. value** is defined so that it delivers the same average power (heating effect) in a resistor as an equivalent steady direct current or voltage.

front_blocks.md: Define a **resistive load**.

back_blocks.md: A **resistive load** is an electrical component with resistance, for example a lamp.

cards.back_md: A **resistive load** is an electrical component with resistance, for example a lamp.

front_blocks.md: How does the mean power delivered to a resistive load compare to the peak power, for a sinusoidal alternating supply?

back_blocks.md: $P_{mean} = \frac{P_{peak}}{2}$
The mean power is **half** the peak (maximum) power.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
For an alternating supply, the power delivered to a resistor is constant with time.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
The power varies constantly with time, since current and voltage are constantly varying; the **mean power** is used as an average measure over a full cycle.
